notes: Observation, not counted as a failure: escape() flattens line breaks to spaces, so ids that differ only by a line-break character (e.g. 'a b' and 'a\nb') collide in prompt_ids in extract.py and a citation lands on the later one. Real ids here are generated (t<seq>) and no such id can arise through the plan's flows; a defensive fix would drop ambiguous citations. Also RollingSummary.text/return value holds unescaped text (possibly a literal </transcript>); it is escaped when re-entering this class's prompt, but any later consumer (T3.x context builder) must escape it too. The full pytest suite was not run to completion (timed out at 120s in the background); only tests/test_memory.py was rerun.
